name: BCF-4
summary: A 282 m truss spine carrying 768 container slots in eight cassette bays, crewed by eighteen from a hammerhead block at the bow. Four drives, two radiator wings, no spin gravity.

rooms.name: Bridge
rooms.description: Five forward stations under raked 19 m glazing, one per watch function: helm, traffic, cargo, power, comms. The ship runs a two-person watch on long legs and all five during approach, docking and cassette transfer. An overhead plot repeats the spine gantry position and every clamp state live. Blast shutters close in 1.8 s; the cab seals and runs on its own 6-hour air supply if the bow block loses pressure.

hotspots.title: Helm Station
hotspots.text: Centre of five forward stations. Helm and traffic share a combined plot during approach.

hotspots.title: Cargo Plot
hotspots.text: Overhead table showing all 768 clamp states and the gantry position, refreshed every 250 ms.

hotspots.title: Raked Glazing
hotspots.text: 19 m of glazing at 22°. The blast shutters close in 1.8 s.

hotspots.title: Captain's Seat
hotspots.text: Behind the helm on the centreline, with repeaters for every station.

rooms.name: Crew Quarters
rooms.description: A 40 m transverse cylinder across the bow, 14 m in diameter. Eighteen bunks in two tiers along the forward wall, each with a 1.9 m³ locker and its own air return. The aft wall carries two heads, a laundry and a 12-seat rec space with the only ports that face the cargo spine. Both ends are pressure doors, so either half isolates in under ten seconds and still holds nine crew.

rooms.name: Galley & Mess
rooms.description: Lower level of the bow block. Three 7 m tables seat all eighteen crew at once, which the watch schedule allows twice a day. The servery runs off a 40 kW induction line and a 22-day chilled store; bulk dry stores ride in two containers in the reefer bay and swap at each port. Lighting drops to 2,700 K at ship's evening. The mess is also the muster point for abandon-ship drills.

hotspots.title: Servery
hotspots.text: 40 kW induction line and a 22-day chilled store behind it.

hotspots.title: Mess Tables
hotspots.text: Three 7 m tables that seat the whole crew of eighteen.

hotspots.title: Circadian Lights
hotspots.text: Ceiling strips that drop from 5,600 K to 2,700 K at ship's evening.

rooms.name: Med Station
rooms.description: Two-bed treatment room aft of the galley with one surgical pod and a cryo cabinet for a single casualty. Most cases run by teleconsult with the destination port; the pod covers stabilisation for up to 72 hours. A recompression chamber for EVA crew sits behind the port bulkhead, rated to 6 bar. Pharmacy stock is sealed and logged by the bridge. The medic is a cross-trained cargo officer.

rooms.name: Docking Collar
rooms.description: Ventral docking port under the bow: an 8 m tunnel ending in an androgynous ring that mates with station collars and crew tenders. A field membrane holds atmosphere while the ring is open, so crew transfer without an airlock cycle. The collar takes 400 kN of docking load; the freighter itself is never berthed. Containers move at the spine by tug and never pass through this port.

rooms.name: Forward Cassettes
rooms.description: Bays five to eight, 136 m of spine. Each bay clamps 96 standard 6 m containers in a plus-shaped section: three wide and two deep on each face, four long. Clamps are hydraulic and individually addressed, so a tug can pull one container without unloading its neighbours. Empty slots are logged and balanced across faces before every burn to hold the centre of mass on the thrust axis.

rooms.name: Aft Cassettes
rooms.description: Bays one to four, closest to the reactor. Hazardous and heavy cargo rides here, where the thrust frame takes the load with the shortest moment arm. Bay frames carry 20 cm of borated polyethylene on the reactor side. The cassettes are unpressurised and unheated; containers that need power plug into a 3 kW umbilical at every clamp position, and draw is metered per slot.

rooms.name: Spine Gantry
rooms.description: A 27 m portal crane that runs the full 274 m of rail along the cassette flanks. It carries a 40 t hoist and a clamp-release tool, and moves containers between bays to trim the ship without calling a tug. Top speed on the rail is 0.6 m/s. The gantry is flown from the bridge cargo station or from a tablet on EVA; nobody rides it under thrust.

rooms.name: Reefer Bay
rooms.description: The port face of bay two, fitted for refrigerated and powered cargo. Each slot carries a 12 kW feed and a data link, and every container reports its temperature to the bridge every 30 s. Contents run from pharmaceuticals and biological samples to the ship's own dry stores. The face holds 22 reefers on a full load; any fault flags the slot amber on the cargo plot.

rooms.name: Reactor Hall
rooms.description: An octagonal hall 26 m across, built round a vertical fusion column in a three-ring confinement stack. Output is 900 MW; the drives take 780 at full burn and the rest feeds the hold and hab. A 1.4-turn shield wall faces the crew end, and the aft side opens to the radiator manifolds. A catwalk rings the column at mid-height. Crew enter the hall only at idle, below 5% throttle.

hotspots.title: Fusion Column
hotspots.text: 18 m vertical column with three confinement rings. 900 MW at full output.

hotspots.title: Confinement Ring
hotspots.text: One of three superconducting rings, kept at 20 K.

hotspots.title: Catwalk
hotspots.text: Mid-height ring walk. Crew may enter only at idle, below 5% throttle.

rooms.name: Radiator Array
rooms.description: Two 44 × 32 m panels on a 104 m transverse boom, set 7° off the boom plane. Liquid tin loops at 1,150 K through nine channels per wing and sheds 520 MW at full power. The panels fold flat against the boom for docking, which the ship always does below 20% throttle to stay inside the reduced heat budget. Micrometeoroid damage isolates one channel at a time.

rooms.name: Drive Cluster
rooms.description: Four magnetoplasma drives on a square thrust frame, 15 m apart. Each develops 1.1 MN, and any three hold a full-load burn at reduced acceleration. The nozzles gimbal ±4° for attitude under thrust, so the bow RCS only works in coast and docking. Burn rating is 140 days continuous. Electrodes are overhauled every third round trip, split between the machine shop and a yard.

rooms.name: Machine Shop
rooms.description: Dorsal workshop over the reactor hall. Two lathes, a 5-axis mill, a metal printer and a bench for drive electrode work. The shop turns any clamp or rail part from stock billet, and repairs most gantry components rather than replacing them. The aft rack holds 3.2 t of spares. Shop air runs through its own filters so metal dust never reaches the hab loop.

hotspots.title: Lathe
hotspots.text: One of two lathes. Turns clamp pins and rail rollers from stock billet.

hotspots.title: Electrode Bench
hotspots.text: Bench for drive electrode refurbishment, with its own fume extraction.

hotspots.title: Spares Rack
hotspots.text: 3.2 t of spares, logged by slot and reordered at every port.

segments.name: Full-Ship Overview
segments.caption: Four hundred and twenty metres, eighteen crew, and 768 container slots. Almost all of the length is cargo.

segments.name: Crew Block
segments.caption: The crew block runs across the bow: 40 m long, eighteen bunks, pressure doors at both ends.

segments.name: Bow & Galley
segments.caption: The bow block holds the galley on its lower level, the med station and the ventral docking collar.

segments.name: Bridge
segments.caption: Five stations under raked glazing. The cargo plot overhead shows every clamp on the spine.

segments.name: Forward Cassettes
segments.caption: Bays five to eight. Each bay clamps 96 containers in a plus-shaped section around the truss.

segments.name: Spine Gantry
segments.caption: The gantry runs the full 274 m of rail and trims the load between burns without a tug.

segments.name: Radiator Array
segments.caption: Two 44 m radiator wings on a transverse boom reject 520 MW of heat through liquid tin.

segments.name: Drive Cluster
segments.caption: Four magnetoplasma drives on a square frame, 4.4 MN together. Any three can hold a full-load burn.

systems.name: Power
systems.description: 900 MW from the reactor hall. The drives take 780 at full burn; the rest runs the length of the spine to the hold umbilicals and the bow.

systems.name: Coolant
systems.description: Liquid tin at 1,150 K from the reactor manifolds out along the boom to nine channels in each radiator wing, and a separate loop through the drive frame.

systems.name: Atmos
systems.description: Air is made in the bow block and reaches engineering through a 1.2 m crawlway in the spine core. The cassette bays are vacuum.

systems.name: Data
systems.description: Cargo plot, clamp states and drive telemetry on a dual fibre ring from the bridge to every bay and the engineering block.
